summary.headline: Sula Q1 FY27 revenue rose 3% to INR121 crore, but gross profit fell 5% as wine-grape mix and adverse market mix cut margins by ~350 bps.
summary.overview: Net revenue from operations grew 3% YoY to INR121 crore (INR118 crore in Q1 FY26), the sixth consecutive month of positive sales growth per management. Elite & Premium grew 6% and Own Brands grew 2%, while Economy & Popular stayed under pressure from competitor discounting. Gross profit fell 5% on a ~150 bps hit from a shift to wine grapes (near 100% of harvest 2026 procurement vs 80% earlier) and a ~200 bps hit from adverse geographic mix. Management says the grape-cost headwind should ease from Q4 FY27 and fully normalise from Q1 FY28, and expects EBITDA margins to recover to last year's levels before FY27 end.

segments.name: Elite & Premium (Own Brands)
segments.commentary: Grew 6% YoY and reached an all-time high 78% share of Own Brands, up 310 bps. The Source and RASA together reached 16% of Own Brands sales, with double-digit growth.

segments.name: Economy & Popular (Own Brands)
segments.commentary: Under pressure from unsustainable competitor discounts; management chose to prioritise Elite & Premium and gave up share here, moderating Own Brands growth.

segments.name: Own Brands (overall)
segments.commentary: Grew 2% YoY. Sula Merlot and Sula Muscat Blanc grew over 100% from a small base; Sula Shiraz Cabernet grew high single digits. These brands are ~45% of Own Brands revenue.

segments.name: Wine Tourism
segments.commentary: Revenue INR15.5 crore, +12% YoY, ~13% of total revenue. Resort occupancy ~63% overall and over 70% excluding The Haven (which was at 43% in Q1).

guidance_outlook: Higher blended grape cost to subside in Q4 FY27 and fully normalise from Q1 FY28, with table grape prices expected to fall meaningfully from harvest 2026 levels.
Management expects table grapes to trade below INR20/kg in harvest 2027, versus INR35/kg peak in harvest 2026 and INR15-16/kg historically.
Expects EBITDA margins to recover to last year's levels shortly and then surpass them, with confidence of achieving this before FY27 end.
Expects net debt to trend lower by end FY27 versus FY26, which should moderate finance costs.
Expects CSD to contribute significantly more than ~4% of FY26 revenue in FY27 after five additional listings; listing completion targeted by Q3 FY27.
Domaine RASA (former Chandon estate, acquired for INR20 crore) winery operations to start in Q4 FY27 with harvest 2027; The Haven profitability expected to improve as occupancy scales from 43%.
Events pavilion (5,000 sq ft) at Nashik on track for Q3 FY27 completion; Domaine Dindori bottle shop opening the following week.
capex_capacity: Amphitheatre expansion at Nashik campus completed in July 2026.
Domaine Dindori bottle shop set to open the week after the call, in line with guidance.

Domain RASA (ex-Chandon estate, Nashik, ~20 minutes from Nashik airport) acquisition completed at INR20 crore; tasting room, bottle shop and banquet facilities already operational; winery operations to start in Q4 FY27.
New 5,000 sq ft events pavilion at Nashik campus on track for Q3 FY27.
Wine Tourism has ~150 keys in total, of which ~70 are owned; the company has not constructed any keys in the last 3-4 years and works on management contracts (minimum tenure ~10 years).
Management is studying building resorts itself in future; Karnataka (Domaine Sula) resort permissions still pending.
demand_pricing: Telangana grew over 50% YoY after route-to-market disruption was resolved in December 2025.
Haryana, Chandigarh, Exports and CSD delivered strong double-digit growth; Karnataka remained soft as the wine category degrew in Q1 and in H2 FY26.
Maharashtra: Elite & Premium resilient; Economy & Popular softer.
Industry: wine category saw little growth over last 2 years, with low single-digit growth per management citing IWSR; excise data is hard to obtain in some states.
Management said Maharashtra's MML policy and Karnataka's excise changes do not apply to wine, with no change in wine duties.
Hot June and delayed monsoon reportedly shifted consumption toward beer in Karnataka and Maharashtra.

qa_highlights.question: Has competition behaved rationally on raw material costs, given the company's 50%+ share of the mass segment, and what is the past behaviour of other players?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cannot guarantee it, but says wine production volumes have been flat to declining as players found the business unsustainable, and table grape prices are expected to fall well below harvest 2026 levels after a more-than-doubling versus prior harvests.

qa_highlights.question: Has the wine industry been flat over the last 3-4 years, and are there plans to diversify into faster-growing categories such as white spirits?
qa_highlights.answer: Wine saw little growth in the last two years per IWSR, with only low single-digit industry growth; excise data is hard to obtain in some states. Management is hopeful the destocking cycle has bottomed, has no white spirits plans now, but has new segments in the pipeline to be detailed later.

qa_highlights.question: Had the grape mix stayed the same, would gross margin have been better or worse, and what is the upside from the mix shift?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin would have been better, since raw material costs would not have risen as they did. Management said it is too early to quantify any upside, but the negative impact will not be present from Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for table grape prices and how far has the blend moved from the strategic mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Table grapes were typically procured at under INR15-16/kg and spiked to about INR35/kg in harvest 2026; prices are expected to fall below INR20/kg. Some sub-INR600 wines now carry 60-70% wine grapes versus the intended almost exclusively table-grape blend.

qa_highlights.question: Do Maharashtra's MML policy or Karnataka's excise changes benefit Sula, and why is Karnataka still weak?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said MML is spirits-only and wine duties are unchanged in both states, so no benefit. Karnataka's weakness is category-wide degrowth in Q1 and H2 FY26; Sula held or gained share in Elite & Premium but lost share in Economy & Popular. Hot June and delayed monsoon shifted some consumption to beer.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital employed and capex per room for Wine Tourism, and what is the lease structure?
qa_highlights.answer: No separate asset base is reported for Wine Tourism; management says its EBITDA margin is better than standalone wine. Of ~150 keys, ~70 are owned, none constructed in the last 3-4 years, and contracts run at least 10 years. Management is studying building its own resorts, so no capex per key was given.

risks_watch: Gross margin recovery depends on table grape prices falling below INR20/kg in harvest 2027; management says this is climate-dependent and not guaranteed.
Economy & Popular pressure from competitor discounting; management has deliberately ceded share there, which may keep Own Brands growth moderate.
Karnataka, a core market, remains soft as the wine category degrew in Q1 and H2 FY26; recovery is expected only in H2 FY27.
Wine Tourism capex strategy shifting toward owned construction; Karnataka resort permissions still pending.
Adverse geographic mix (~200 bps gross margin hit) may persist as lower-margin markets grow faster; EBITDA impact is cushioned by lower selling costs.
Watch CSD listings (five additional brands, completion targeted by Q3 FY27) and Domaine RASA winery start in Q4 FY27 as the next quarter's milestones.
key_quotes: Importantly, this marks six consecutive months of positive sales growth, giving us confidence that the business has returned to a path of consistent growth.
Importantly, this is not structural, but we believe just a temporary phenomenon.
We expect to recover to last year's EBITDA margin levels shortly and then hopefully surpass them.
Wine is quite different than spirits.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the top line and Wine Tourism, and specific about timelines for grape-cost normalisation. Cautious and hedged on the grape price outlook, with explicit caveats that certainty is limited and outcomes depend on climate. Evasive on Wine Tourism capital employed and per-room capex, which it did not quantify.

adds.what: Domaine RASA winery operations (ex-Chandon estate, Nashik) starting with harvest 2027; tasting room, bottle shop and banquet already operational
5,000 sq ft events pavilion at Nashik campus (wine tourism)
Five additional CSD listings (route-to-market, not productive capacity)

growth.why: Management gives no explicit revenue growth figure; Q1 revenue rose 3% with Elite & Premium up 6%, and EBITDA margins are guided to recover to last year's levels before FY27 end as grape costs ease from Q4 FY27, backed partly by Domaine RASA winery start (harvest 2027), CSD listings and the events pavilion, though the margin guidance rests mostly on cost normalisation rather than volume capacity.
